summary: Ekyo Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a research fellow at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).

Eleanor Nesbitt works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1970–1973) and the University of Oxford (~1973–1974), later becoming emerita professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989).

Eleanor Rosch is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her bachelor's at Reed College and her Ph.D. at Harvard under Roger Brown, later holding posts at Brown University and UC Berkeley (from 1971).

Elena De Rossi Filibeck specializes in Tibetology. She studied East Asian history under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome (graduated by 1971) and held posts at Sapienza University (Associate Professor from 1980) and the University of Bonn (~1981–1983).
Elena France Hanson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey.

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen. She held positions at the University of Tübingen (2016–2017, ~2017–2022) and became Assistant Professor and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tel Aviv, EPHE, Paris Nanterre under Charles Malamoud, and Hamburg, and held posts at La Trobe, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig University (2004–2021).

Elijah Sacvan Ary is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2001–2007), completing his PhD under supervisors Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Eliot Deutsch was a philosophy and Indology scholar. Educated at Wisconsin-Madison and Columbia (Ph.D. 1960), he taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1967–2006) and editor of Philosophy East and West.

Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2006). She has held positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Sapienza University of Rome, and the University of Vienna (~2012–2021).

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar. Educated at Würzburg and Münster, she held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (from 1988), also serving as SBL president (1987–1988).

Elizabeth A. Cecil works in Indology, religious studies, and archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown under James L. Fitzgerald and held posts at the University of Groningen, Leiden University, and Florida State University (~2018).

Elizabeth Anne Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed her doctoral studies under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She held teaching appointments at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth De Michelis is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her master's at SOAS and her PhD at the University of Cambridge, where she served as director from 2000, later joining the theology faculty at Oxford.
Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.

Elizabeth Errington is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar. In 1993, she became curator of pre-Islamic coins of South and Central Asia at the British Museum.

Elizabeth Guthrie works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Canterbury (~1997) and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya, supervised by Ananda Guruge and Y. Karunadasa, later working at Birmingham (~2014).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978) and held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
